name: Eyes & colour

overlay.caption: staring at red → red-sensing cells tire → white looks green until they recover

does: Shows colour-sensing cells tiring the longer they stare at one colour
Shows the afterimage being the opposite colour and growing stronger with longer staring
Shows the effect fading as the cells recover
doesnt: Measure any real person — the numbers are illustrative teaching values
Cover colour blindness or how colour is processed in the brain in detail
Suggest staring at bright lights or the sun — never do that
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: Afterimages from paint or paper fade in seconds. If spots in your vision don't fade, tell an adult.

sources: NIH National Eye Institute: how the eyes work (student pages)
